rows.core: Sol'Kanar leverages donating cursed permanents after extracting their early benefits; Demonic Pact and Illusions/Gambit liabilities must transfer safely and at the right timing.
rows.positive: Commander's Sphere provides mana of any commander-identity color and sacrifices to draw a card, smoothing early color access to cast donation and curse spells.
rows.cut_cost: Spiteful Banditry doubles as a scalable damage-to-creatures sweeper and repeatable opponent-death Treasure producer, clearing hostile boards without relinquishing the donated-permanent win plan.
rules: Sol'Kanar's donation package depends on who controls the liability when its trigger resolves, not just which player originally owned it.
Spiteful Banditry's enter trigger deals X damage to all creatures; X must be paid at cast time.
Spiteful Banditry creates a Treasure when one or more creatures an opponent controls die, but only once each turn.
Commander's Sphere costs three and normally taps for a color in the commander's identity, with a separate sacrifice-to-draw ability.
Neither mana fixing nor an independent X-sweeper directly removes Demonic Pact's lose-game choice; actual transfer timing still governs safety.
rows.adverse: The replacement removes a source of emergency board control and Treasures for a generic three-mana ramp cantrip already redundant with other rocks.
rows.followup: Trace one genuine Pact donation and opposing creature-board reset with Banditry versus Sphere, including exact mana/priority and loss-trigger ownership.

rows.core: Demon tribal wins from Be'lakor's Demon-entry damage proportional to power and commander ETB draw for Demon count; cheap cantrips are secondary to actual Demon arrivals.
rows.positive: Brainstorm offers one-blue instant card selection, improves keeping expensive Demons castable and can combine with shuffles before a big Be'lakor turn.
rows.cut_cost: Unholy Annex // Ritual Chamber is a Demon-adjacent source of repeatable draw, pressure and potentially an additional Demon permanent, which advances the tribal entry-damage plan.
rules: Be'lakor's damage trigger requires another Demon entering under your control and uses that Demon's power.
Be'lakor's enter-the-battlefield draw depends on the number of Demon permanents as the trigger resolves, not Brainstorm's number of cards drawn.
Brainstorm draws three and puts two hand cards on top; without a shuffle or new draw engine it can preserve uncastable expensive cards on top.
Room halves are independently unlocked by paying their costs; an uncast half has no active rules text.
Replacing a Demon-specific repeatable Room with one-shot selection may lower commander-native triggers and persistent pressure.
rows.adverse: A cheap cantrip may improve a marginal starting hand, but losing a Demon-relevant permanent risks both value and Be'lakor threat density.
rows.followup: Compare archived source Demon-permanent count and Be'lakor ETB/damage output with Room versus Brainstorm across source-shuffle openings.

rows.core: Rat arrivals grow a Snail token whose power can be sacrificed to Wick for damage to every opponent and cards; Rat/Snail type changes plus free sacrifice loops are central.
rows.positive: Dimir Signet is a two-mana U/B filter, easing Wick's {U}{B}{R} activation color burden in some two-color-heavy hands.
rows.cut_cost: Pitiless Plunderer converts non-Plunderer creature deaths into Treasures, an engine for repeat Rat fodder, Snail sacrifice and multi-activation color supply.
rules: Wick's activated ability requires sacrificing a Snail as part of its cost, so that permanent is gone before the effect resolves.
Pitiless Plunderer triggers whenever another creature under its controller's control dies, producing a Treasure; it can provide resources after a sacrificed Snail dies.
Dimir Signet generates {U}{B} only with an additional generic input and cannot supply the {R} Wick still needs.
Changing the Snail's creature type to Rat can create arrival triggers through other effects only if the creature actually enters; existing Snail type changes are not fresh entry.
Replacing a sacrificial death-payoff with a mana-filter rock can break otherwise source-supported commander-native resource loops.
rows.adverse: The Signet smooths mana but loses a death-trigger Treasure engine, a particularly costly sacrifice-economy card in Wick's actual strategy.
rows.followup: Model a real Snail sacrifice turn and Rat/Snail type-change loop with Plunderer and without, including exact Treasure, black and red payments.

rows.core: The returned Lord pays an ETB cost with three creatures, life and opponent cards, then converts every creature sacrifice into an extra card; dedicated fodder and mana loops are protected.
rows.positive: Rakdos Signet can accelerate a two-colored part of the five-mana commander's cost and facilitate early sacrifice outlets when colors are awkward.
rows.cut_cost: Mahadi, Emporium Master converts creatures that died this turn into end-step Treasure, turning the Lord's initial fodder sacrifice and later token kills into persistent mana.
rules: Tresserhorn's Lord requires sacrificing three creatures, paying three life and granting target opponent three cards to avoid its enter-trigger sacrifice.
His own sacrifice-draw trigger pays off each creature you sacrifice, making additional creature-death mana payoffs strategically relevant.
Mahadi, Emporium Master's end-step trigger counts creatures that died that turn and makes Treasures, provided Mahadi is controlled and the triggering condition is satisfied.
Rakdos Signet needs an extra generic mana input to tap for {B}{R}; it produces no creature fodder or death trigger.
The source marks this commander as project-authorized future-release, not officially Commander-legal before November 13, 2026.
rows.adverse: A Signet offers earlier filtering at the price of a payoff converting the three-creature ETB liability into Treasure; its life/card engine lacks this compensation.
rows.followup: Trace legal ETB with three actual fodder creatures, resulting Lord draws and Mahadi's later Treasure count versus Signet opening casts; maintain future-release status.

rows.core: Connecting Obeka creates extra upkeep steps proportional to combat damage, multiplying upkeep-based draw, artifact, counter and token engines; priority is reliable damage.
rows.positive: Izzet Signet may offer dependable U/R filtering in games where opponents lack suitable colored lands for Fellwar Stone.
rows.cut_cost: Fellwar Stone is a two-mana rock that typically taps immediately for a color an opponent land could produce, and does not require an additional mana payment each time.
rules: Obeka gains additional upkeep steps after dealing combat damage to a player; she does not obtain extra turns or combat phases.
Izzet Signet's mana ability requires paying {1} and tapping it to add {U}{R}; one Signet plus no other mana cannot activate.
Fellwar Stone's available colors depend on what lands opponents control, not on its owner's commander's color identity.
Neither rock directly makes Obeka unblockable, raises combat damage or creates an upkeep-value trigger.
The choice depends on opponent land-color coverage and early usable source sequences, not a generic preferred Signet ranking.
rows.adverse: Signet trades flexible single-source access for two-colored output requiring upfront mana, a fragile fit for protecting an aggressive three-color commander.
rows.followup: Simulate real multiplayer opponent land colors and T2-T4 Obeka deployments, measuring payable upkeep engines with both rocks.

rows.core: Zevlor activates {2}, {T}, and then the next single-target instant or sorcery aimed at one opponent or their permanent can be copied to other opponents, turning high-impact targeted spells into multiplayer value.
rows.positive: Resonating Lute grants each land an additional tap ability for two mana of any one color, restricted to instant or sorcery SPELL casts. This can fund Zevlor's expensive targeted payloads in later turns.
rows.cut_cost: Dark Ritual supplies three black mana for one black instant, powering an earlier Zevlor activation plus targeted payoff or a protected table-wide spell turn.
rules: Zevlor's {2}, {T} activation is an activated ability; Resonating Lute's added land mana is restricted to CASTING instant or sorcery spells, so cannot pay this cost.
Resonating Lute costs {2}{U}{R}; lands you control can tap for two mana of one color restricted to casting instants/sorceries, not ordinary untap or permanents.
Resonating Lute's own tap ability draws a card only if seven or more cards are in hand when activated.
The spell that Zevlor later copies must have an appropriate single opponent/opponent-permanent target; neither Lute nor mana generation automatically fulfills its target restriction.
Dark Ritual adds {B}{B}{B} for {B}, providing immediate black acceleration even when Zevlor's delayed-copy ability costs two generic mana.
rows.adverse: Lute costs four and its restricted land mana cannot pay Zevlor's {2} activated ability or the commander creature spell. Replacing Dark Ritual's immediate three black mana delays early Zevlor-plus-payload turns.
rows.followup: Run two paired source-paid Zevlor targeted spells with Lute on field and actual untapped lands, keeping Zevlor's {2} separate from spell-casting mana; compare Dark Ritual fast-turn payoff.
rows.next: Run two paired source-paid Zevlor targeted spells with Lute on field and actual untapped lands, keeping Zevlor's {2} separate from spell-casting mana; compare Dark Ritual fast-turn payoff.
